title: Whether there is faith in demons
pass_a_gloss: Article XI. Whether there is faith in demons. 1. The question is whether demons have faith. Scripture says, James 2:19, the demons believe and tremble. From this it is gathered that some faith is in them. 2. Yet a distinction must be made: the faith which is in demons is historical or dogmatic faith — the intellect's assent to the truth of what God has revealed — not justifying or fiducial faith. They believe that God is, and that many things about Christ are true; but they do not rest on Christ as Savior, nor love God. 3. Hence Augustine and the Scholastics: the demons' faith is without love and without trust; therefore it is dead and does not contribute to salvation. Saving faith is "formed" by charity (as they speak), or rather is inseparable from charity and trust in adults. 4. Bonaventure and others ask whether the demons' faith is an infused habit of faith. We answer that it is rather knowledge acquired from experience and revelations, not a habit of grace; for sanctifying grace is not in demons.
pass_b_english: Article XI. Whether there is faith in demons.
1. Do demons have faith? James 2:19 — the demons believe and tremble — shows some faith is in them.

2. Distinguish: theirs is historical or dogmatic faith — intellective assent to what God revealed — not justifying or fiducial faith. They believe that God is and that much about Christ is true; they do not rest on Christ as Savior or love God.
3. So Augustine and the Scholastics: demons' faith is without love and trust — dead, and of no avail for salvation. Saving faith in adults is inseparable from charity and trust.
4. Is demons' faith an infused habit? Rather it is knowledge from experience and revelations, not a habit of grace — sanctifying grace is not in them.
source_text:
ART. XI.
An in Daemonibus sit fides.

1. Quaeritur an daemones fidem habeant. Scriptura dicit, Jacob.2.19. daemones credunt & contremiscunt. Unde colligitur iis inesse aliquam fidem.

2. Distinguendum tamen est: fides quae daemonibus inest, est fides historica seu dogmatica — assensus intellectus de veritate eorum quae DEUS revelavit — non fides justificans seu fiducialis. Credunt DEUM esse, & multa de CHRISTO vera esse; sed non recumbunt in CHRISTUM ut Salvatorem, nec amant DEUM.

3. Unde Augustinus & Scholastici: fides daemonum est sine dilectione & sine fiducia; ideoque mortua est, & ad salutem non confert. Fides salvifica formatur charitate (ut loquuntur), seu potius a charitate & fiducia inseparabilis est in adultis.

4. Bonaventura & alii quaerunt an fides daemonum sit fidei habitus infusus. Respondemus eam potius esse notitiam acquisitam ex experientia & revelationibus, non habitum gratiae; nam gratia sanctificans daemonibus non inest.
